output.summary: The deterministic verdict is NO_POLICY for both policy windows (reference and evaluation): the window policy summaries report business_verdict NO_POLICY, resource_verdict NO_POLICY, and verdict NO_POLICY, and the analysis-level policy verdict is NO_POLICY. The run is VALID and analysis coverage is COMPLETE. Observed load was error-free (0 errors overall and in both windows) with stable latency (overall p50 198 ms, p95 237 ms, p99 239 ms; reference p50 192 ms / p95 233 ms; evaluation p50 200 ms / p95 238 ms) at a constant target of 20 requests/s. The correlation diagnostic tested all 16 resource series against response_time_p95_ms and selected two candidates after Holm adjustment: resource-00 (rho 0.974643 at lag 0) and resource-06 (rho 0.376900 at lag 0), both status CANDIDATE with uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED. Because clock alignment is not verified by core and only lag 0 was examined, these are hypotheses, not causes. NO_POLICY is preserved; the candidates do not change the verdict.

hypotheses.observation: In the evaluation window, correlation pair-00 (resource-00 vs response_time_p95_ms) reports raw/partial rho 0.974643 at best_lag_ms 0, status CANDIDATE, uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, and the headline selection was SELECTED with Holm-adjusted p 0.016.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: resource-00 utilization and p95 response time move together at zero lag in this window; this is a statistical association and could reflect a shared load profile or a confounder rather than a direct relationship.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the raw resource-00 and p95 latency series in the evaluation window; verify clock alignment between the load generator and resource telemetry before attributing the association, and consider a lag search across nonzero offsets.

hypotheses.observation: Correlation pair-06 (resource-06 vs response_time_p95_ms) reports raw/partial rho 0.376900 at best_lag_ms 0, status CANDIDATE, uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, and was SELECTED with Holm-adjusted p 0.016.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: resource-06 shows a weaker but statistically selected association with p95 latency; the association may be driven by part of the window or by the same shared load pattern observed for other series.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Plot resource-06 against p95 latency per cell and check whether the association is stable across the evaluation window; confirm clocks and rerun with a varying load profile to test the association under different load.

hypotheses.observation: The target series is constant at 20 requests/s in both windows (min=max=mean=median=20, sample_standard_deviation 0, slope 0), and every correlation pair lists controls_requested ['target'], controls_dropped ['target'], controls_used [] with reason CONSTANT_CONTROL.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A constant control provides no variance to partial out, so the reported partial rho equals raw rho and the correlations are unadjusted for load.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun with a non-constant target/load profile so the load control is usable for partial correlation and so sensitivity estimates can be obtained.

hypotheses.observation: Both window policy summaries report verdict NO_POLICY with business_verdict NO_POLICY and resource_verdict NO_POLICY; the analysis-level policy verdict is NO_POLICY.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: No applicable business policy rule and no resource rule with effect sla existed for these windows, so the product cannot produce PASS or FAIL; the error-free and constant-load metrics do not change that.
hypotheses.recommended_check: If a PASS/FAIL assertion on latency or resource usage is desired, define the applicable business policy rule and resource SLA rules, then rerun the analysis so the product evaluates them.

hypotheses.observation: resource-binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core, and the correlation pairs tested only a single lag_profile entry at lag_ms 0 (best_lag_ms 0).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Without verified clock alignment and with only zero lag examined, any lead/lag or temporal ordering between resource and latency series is unsupported.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clocks across the load generator, sampling, and resource telemetry first; only after verification, run a lag search across a range of offsets.

hypotheses.observation: The diagnostic summary is COMPLETE with pairs_tested 16 and pairs_evaluable 16, but anomalies_tested is 0 and episodes_reported is 0; uncertainty is NOT_ESTIMATED.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The diagnostic exercised the correlation method but reported no anomaly episodes; with a constant 20 requests/s load profile, absence of reported episodes does not by itself prove stability or absence of a problem.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect per-cell resource and latency series directly for step changes, and consider a rerun with varied load or longer duration so the anomaly path has signal to test.

hypotheses.observation: Overall and transaction summaries report 0 errors across 7200 samples with latency p50 198, p95 237, p99 239, max 240 ms; the reference window summary reports 0 errors over 2400 samples and the evaluation window 0 errors over 4800 samples.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The run is error-free at the reported aggregation, but this does not imply health against any SLA because no policy thresholds were evaluated in this NO_POLICY verdict.
hypotheses.recommended_check: If latency or error limits matter, encode them in a business policy rule so the product can evaluate the run against them.

hypotheses.observation: p50 latency is 192 ms in the reference window and 200 ms in the evaluation window; p95 is 233 ms vs 238 ms and max latency is 239 ms vs 240 ms.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: There may be a small upward shift in mid-latency across windows, but with no evaluated policy and a constant 20 requests/s target this is not classified as a failure and could reflect noise or measurement timing.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Compare per-cell latency distributions across the two windows and verify timestamps and clocks before treating the shift as meaningful.

recommendations.action: Keep the deterministic verdict NO_POLICY for both windows and treat the two selected correlation pairs (resource-00, resource-06) as candidate hypotheses only, not as a pass, failure, or proven cause.
recommendations.rationale: The product reports NO_POLICY when no applicable business policy rule and no resource rule with effect sla exists for the windows; healthy-looking metrics do not turn NO_POLICY into PASS.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment between the load generator, sampling, and resource telemetry before interpreting any correlation, since clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core and only lag 0 was tested.
recommendations.rationale: An unverified clock relationship cannot support lead/lag ordering or a temporal causal hypothesis; only after verification can a lag search across offsets be meaningful.

recommendations.action: Inspect the raw resource-00 and resource-06 series against p95 latency in the evaluation window before drawing conclusions from the rho values.
recommendations.rationale: Both candidates carry uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED and sensitivity_without_achieved_rps null, so no effect size or confidence is quantified; direct series inspection bounds the claim.

recommendations.action: If a PASS/FAIL assertion on latency or capacity is required, define the applicable business policy rule and resource rules with effect sla, then rerun the analysis.
recommendations.rationale: Without product-evaluated rules the verdict for these windows remains NO_POLICY; only rules the product evaluates can yield PASS or FAIL.

recommendations.action: Rerun with a non-constant load profile so the target control is not dropped as CONSTANT_CONTROL and partial correlations and sensitivity can be meaningfully estimated.
recommendations.rationale: All correlation pairs dropped the target as CONSTANT_CONTROL and used no controls, making partial rho equal to raw rho and unadjusted for load; load variation would allow a usable control.

recommendations.action: Communicate NO_POLICY semantics to consumers: the run is neither PASS nor FAIL because no applicable rule was evaluated, regardless of the error-free and stable-looking metrics.
recommendations.rationale: Missing policy is not a pass; reporting the constant 20 requests/s load or zero errors as a green result would misstate the deterministic verdict.

caveats: Clock alignment is not verified by core; best_lag_ms is 0 and only a single lag profile entry at lag_ms 0 was tested, so no lead/lag or temporal causal ordering is supported.
Both selected correlation candidates carry uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED and sensitivity_without_achieved_rps null, so no effect size or confidence interval is quantified.
The target control was constant (20 requests/s, sample_standard_deviation 0, slope 0) and was dropped in every correlation pair; the reported partial rho equals the raw rho and is unadjusted.
NO_POLICY for both windows means no business policy rule and no resource rule with effect sla was evaluated; it is not a PASS, even though the run metrics look healthy.
Overall run counts (7200 samples) and per-window counts (2400 reference, 4800 evaluation) are different scopes with different denominators and are not directly comparable.
anomalies_tested is 0 and episodes_reported is 0 in a COMPLETE diagnostic; absence of reported anomaly episodes is not proof of stability, spare capacity, or absence of a problem.
The run extends 180 ms past the evaluation end (run_to_epoch_ms 1767225960180 vs evaluation_to_epoch_ms 1767225960000), leaving a small trailing remainder outside the evaluation window.

resource-binding reports one evaluation window from run start (1767225600000) to 1767225960000, while the window policy and metric summaries split that span into a 120-second reference and a 240-second evaluation sub-window; verify window definitions before comparing.
The 14 non-selected correlation pairs did not reject the Holm-adjusted tests; that is not evidence that those resources are unrelated to latency.
Latency percentiles in the reference vs evaluation window (p50 192 vs 200 ms, p95 233 vs 238 ms) differ slightly, but no threshold was evaluated because the verdict is NO_POLICY.
